stem: A 32-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of aching and swelling in her hands and wrists for the past 10 days. She reports that the symptoms are symmetric and primarily affect the proximal interphalangeal and metacarpal joints. She describes a brief period of stiffness in the morning that resolves within 15 minutes. She has no significant past medical history and takes no medications. Her only recent change is that she began volunteering at a local daycare center three weeks ago. Vitals are: temperature 37.1°C, pulse 72/min, blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, respiratory rate 14/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air. Physical examination shows mild swelling and tenderness of the second and third MCP joints bilaterally. Laboratory studies show a normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein. Rheumatoid factor is negative.
lead_in: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: The patient presents with an acute, symmetric polyarthritis of the small joints of the hands, associated with an exposure to children (daycare), and a brief period of morning stiffness (<30 minutes). Normal inflammatory markers (ESR/CRP) and the acute onset strongly favor a viral etiology over an autoimmune process. Parvovirus B19 often presents this way in adults, mimicking rheumatoid arthritis (RA), but the course is self-limited. RA typically features prolonged morning stiffness (>30 minutes), elevated ESR/CRP, and a chronic progressive course. Erythema infectiosum refers to the childhood rash (slapped cheek) associated with Parvovirus B19, but the adult presentation is predominantly articular. SLE would typically present with other systemic features (rash, renal issues) and elevated inflammatory markers.
teaching_point: Adults with Parvovirus B19 infection often present with a symmetric polyarthritis mimicking rheumatoid arthritis, distinguished by brief morning stiffness, normal ESR/CRP, and exposure to children.

distractor_rationale.A: This is the name of the pediatric rash manifestation, not the adult arthritic syndrome.
distractor_rationale.C: This occurs in children, not 32-year-old adults.
distractor_rationale.D: RA presents with prolonged morning stiffness and elevated ESR/CRP.
distractor_rationale.E: SLE usually involves multisystem organ involvement and elevated inflammatory markers.
